title: FAQs: Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator | NHSN | CDC
content: FAQs: Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator Print Minus Related Pages On This Page Participation Overview NHSN Access Reporting Requirements Data & Data Use Participation Overview 1. What do I need to do to participate? To report the NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator, facilities must be enrolled in NHSN and have elected to follow the Patient Safety Component. If you are uncertain about your facility’s NHSN enrollment status, your facility’s infection prevention staff are a great resource for this information. Using the facility’s Center for Medicare & Medicaid Services number (CCN), enrollment status can be checked at https://nhsn.cdc.gov/AMIE/ . If you are still unsure about your facility’s NHSN enrollment status, contact NHSN@cdc.gov with “NHSN Enrollment Status” in the subject line. Include the facility’s name, address, and CCN in the email. 2. We have multiple facilities within our health system. May we select which facilities participate in the early reporting of the Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator? Yes, any facility that is eligible to enroll in the Patient Safety Component may report the NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator. The facility must have a critical care unit/location as one of their active locations within the NHSN application. 3. Which units are eligible for reporting nurse staffing hours to NHSN? Facilities may report all their critical units that have been mapped in NHSN. This includes pediatric critical units as well as neonatal critical care units. 4. Our hospital has several critical care units/locations. May we select which critical care units/locations participate in the early reporting of the Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator? If a facility elects to report the NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator, all critical care units/locations which are in active status within the NHSN application must be reported. 5. Where are the NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator protocol and training materials located? The protocol and training materials can be found on the NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator webpage at https://www.cdc.gov/nhsn/psc/nshi/index.html . NHSN Access 6. My facility is currently not enrolled in NHSN but would like to report Nurse Staffing Hours. How do we enroll in NHSN? Facility enrollment information can be found at https://www.cdc.gov/nhsn/enrollment/index.html . 7. Will the NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours data be entered using a different portal than the main NDNQI (National Database for Nursing Quality Indicators) data entry portal? Yes, the NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator data must be entered into the NHSN application. 8. In my role at my facility, I do not have access to NHSN. If we elect to participate, would I send our critical care nursing care hours to our infection control practitioner? Each facility must decide the appropriate workflow for reporting the Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator. The NHSN Facility Administrator within your facility may add additional users to report these data. We recommend that facilities discuss this internally so individuals can complete the necessary steps to access the NHSN application. Reporting Requirements 9. Is the reporting of nurse staffing hours and patient days similar to those reported to NDNQI or are there additional data elements? The data elements for the NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator are similar to those reported to NDNQI and are based on measures stewarded by the American Nurses Association, which are endorsed by a consensus-based entity. #0204 – Skill mix (Registered Nurse [RN], Licensed Vocational/Practical Nurse [LVN/LPN], unlicensed assistive personnel [UAP], and contract) #0205 – Nursing Hours per Patient Day 10. Are contract staff included in the nurse staffing hours totals? Nursing staff in the categories of RN, LPN/LVN and UAP working more than 50% of the shift and providing direct patient care on a critical care unit mapped to NHSN are eligible to be counted, regardless of employment classifications (such as full-time, part-time, PRN, contract, staff pulled from another unit). 11. Are the nurse staffing hours data reported yearly or monthly? The NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator are reported as a monthly total for each nurse staffing role: registered nurses (RNs), licensed vocational/practical nurses (LVN/LPN) and unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP). 12. Will the full implementation be restricted to only critical care units? Additional units/locations will be added in the future, but a timeframe has not yet been determined. 13. Will the new indicator continue to be voluntary? At this time, reporting NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator will be voluntary. Users will be notified in advance of any changes. Data & Data Use 14. Do you have an example of what data analysis reports will look like? Currently, there are no sample reports. Available metrics include Total Nurse Staffing Hours per Patient Day, and Nurse Staffing Hours separated for each nursing category (RN, LPN/LVN, UAP), as well as Percentage of Productive Hours Worked by RNs, LPN/LVNs, and UAPs. 15. Will the indicator be used to evaluate the impact of Nurse Staffing Hours and HAIs? As adequate NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours data become available, NHSN anticipates evaluating these data alongside HAI data. Facilities entering these data are encouraged to perform analysis of these data at the facility-, CDC location code-, location-, and location type-levels. Overtime, facilities can use these data to monitor for trends and track the impact of prevention strategies. 16. Would we receive any different or additional reports or information than that received from NDNQI, such as a correlation between Nurse Staffing Hours and infection rates? NHSN intends to assess any associations between nurse staffing metrics and HAI incidence rates when sufficient reporting exists. Furthermore, these new metrics will be included together with other potential explanatory factors when assessing them for independent association with HAI incidence rates. Descriptive analyses will be performed on these metrics and NHSN will provide reports that help facilities characterize the distributions of these metrics across the various patient care locations from which they are reported within each facility. 17. How are the data entered? The NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours data may be entered manually. The .CSV upload option will be available after October 21, 2023. 18. What are the data elements, and how frequently are the elements reported? The data elements for the NHSN Nurse Staffing Hours Indicator are total direct care hours for each of the nurse staffing roles – registered nurses (RNs), licensed vocational/practical nurses (LVN/LPN) and unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP), as well as total patient day counts. All data elements should be reported from the same critical care unit/location.
